clue.text: Small group getting over instrumentalist

definitions.note: the instrument stands for its player, as an orchestra speaks of 'the cellos'

blocks.note: a cell is a small group, e.g. of activists
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A little band of players wins over a solo musician.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses the instrument for the person playing it, as orchestras do when they say 'the cellos came in late'.
explanation.definitionFit: By metonymy the bowed string instrument names its player, so a cello in an orchestra can be a musician.

clue.text: Turns up on the edge of racetrack area offering positions for drivers

indicators.note: a word placed on the edges of another sits at both its ends, enclosing it

blocks.note: to cock a hat brim or an ear is to turn it up
the pit is the servicing area beside a motor-racing track

explanation.surface: Things raised at the trackside give racing drivers their seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists, but racing and the wordplay both point to cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockpit is the compartment where a racing driver or pilot sits to control the vehicle.

clue.text: Don't mess with holidays, getting place for night, not day

indicators.note: not means without, so the abbreviation for day is taken out

blocks.note: leave is time off work
where one sleeps at night

explanation.surface: Telling someone on holiday to keep away from a hotel room booked by night rather than day.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the standard abbreviation for day.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something be is to let it alone and not interfere, an idiom for not tampering with it.

clue.text: Tournament seems to struggle without a way to dissolve barriers

indicators.note: a word that struggles writhes about, so its letters are twisted into a new order
without in its old sense of outside, so one piece lies outside the other

blocks.note: an open is a tournament anyone may enter, as in golf or tennis
anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports tournament seems to falter for lack of a way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is not 'lacking' here but 'outside', so the rearranged letters surround the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba's magic password opened the robbers' cave, and the phrase now means any sure way past obstacles.

clue.text: Long-standing foe, heartless, as seen in historical records

indicators.note: losing the heart means the central letter of the phrase is dropped

blocks.note: an arch-rival is a long-standing chief enemy

explanation.surface: An old enemy, cold and cruel, turns up in the history books.
explanation.walkthrough: ARCHRIVAL has nine letters, so its heart is the fifth, the R, which goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Archival describes what belongs to or is found in archives, which are collections of historical records.

clue.text: Company engaged by one actor in adapting further establishment

indicators.note: something engaged by another is taken on and held within it
adapting means changing to fit, so these combined letters are altered into a new arrangement

blocks.note: a firm is a business company
taken as written for the fodder

explanation.surface: A theatre company signs up a single performer while adapting a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a theatre troupe but is a business. Since everything is shuffled, where the firm sits among the other letters does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconfirmation is a further act of establishing or verifying something already confirmed.

clue.text: Sacred loch in Orkney island

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so it sits within the island's name

blocks.note: Hoy is one of the Orkney islands off northern Scotland
L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: A holy lake set on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy and sacred are synonyms, both meaning dedicated to God or a religious purpose.

clue.text: A lot of poetry, very popular, gaining nothing in translation

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the final letter is cut
a word gaining something takes it inside itself

blocks.note: verse is poetry
in means fashionable or popular
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Much verse, however well loved, loses its sense when translated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very popular' together stands for IN, the word for being fashionable; 'nothing' goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A version is a rendering of a text in another language, so a translation.

clue.text: Remiss to clothe half of team in rubbery material

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only part of it, so its second half is removed
clothing something wraps around it, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: lax means careless or remiss
only its first half is kept

explanation.surface: Forgetting to dress half the squad in rubber kit.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex is the milky sap of rubber trees or its synthetic equivalent, used for gloves and balloons.

clue.text: Father blocking rude behaviour – there's a line to be drawn here

definitions.text: there's a line to be drawn here

indicators.note: something blocking a path stands in the middle of it, so it goes inside the phrase

blocks.note: vulgar means rude and an action is behaviour
FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A priest puts a stop to bad conduct and says some lines may not be crossed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A line to be drawn' sounds like a moral limit; it is the bar between numerator and denominator.
explanation.definitionFit: A vulgar fraction is written with numerator over denominator, separated by a horizontal line.

clue.text: Two varieties of the same drink united vineyard estate

blocks.clueFragment: Two varieties of the same drink
blocks.note: CHA and TEA are both words for the drink tea
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Two kinds of the same beverage get mixed at a wine-growing property.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is a British slang word for tea, borrowed from Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: A château is a French wine-producing estate, named after the country house at its centre.

clue.text: Being at fault, Parisian is abandoning religious leader in fake religion

definitions.note: read as a noun: a being who is at fault

indicators.note: something abandoning another thing leaves it behind, so those letters are removed from the leader's title
one piece sits inside the other, so the cult wraps around what remains

blocks.note: a cult is a sect often seen as a false religion
est is French for 'is'
a priest leads worship

explanation.surface: Someone in the wrong walks away from a cleric to join a bogus sect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being at fault' looks like a phrase about a state; the being is a person, the guilty party.
explanation.definitionFit: A culprit is the person responsible for a wrongdoing, so a being who is at fault.

clue.text: Encourage man to secure a PR rep

indicators.note: securing something holds it in place, so the single letter is held between the other pieces

blocks.note: to press someone is to urge them on
taken as written
short for gentleman

explanation.surface: Urging a fellow to hire a public relations representative.
explanation.definitionFit: A press agent handles publicity for a client, which is the work of a public relations representative.

clue.text: Source of justice in a social media platform? It's a bad influence

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: first letter of justice
taken as written
X is the platform formerly called Twitter

explanation.surface: A jab at a social network: its effect on fairness is malign.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinx is a person or thing thought to bring bad luck, a malign influence on events.

clue.text: Instrument beginning to capture former pop group in Debussy classic

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word is its first letter alone
the band goes in the orchestral work, inside its title

blocks.note: first letter of capture
La Mer is Debussy's orchestral piece about the sea
Wham! was the 1980s duo of George Michael and Andrew Ridgeley

explanation.surface: A musical instrument begins to catch an old pop act playing Debussy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a clue full of music, 'Instrument' means a tool, not something you play.
explanation.definitionFit: A claw hammer is a tool, an implement, with a split back for pulling out nails.

clue.text: Auntie reads RLS novel – this one?

indicators.note: novel also means new, so the letters before it are made into something new

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: An aunt is reading a Stevenson book, and we are asked which one.
explanation.walkthrough: RLS is Robert Louis Stevenson. 'Novel' does double duty: it signals the rearrangement and, with the whole clue, defines the book.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 pirate adventure, his most famous novel.

clue.text: Intrinsic qualities enclosed in letters

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, so it sits within it

blocks.note: esses are the letter S written out, plural
ENC is the abbreviation written on letters with something enclosed

explanation.surface: The heart of things is tucked inside written correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests post, which fits ENC, but it means letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An essence is the fundamental nature or quality that makes a thing what it is.

clue.text: Wait and see what I say to the examiner

definitions.text: what I say to the examiner

blocks.note: first meaning: a warning that events will prove the speaker right

blocks.clueFragment: what I say to the examiner
blocks.note: second meaning: read literally, a candidate asking an examiner to grade their written answers

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the phrase taken literally: an examiner marks the words a candidate writes.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is a prediction that one will be proved right, and literally it is a request to grade one's script.

clue.text: Name of complex notion mostly thrown up in work

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
thrown up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so backwards
placed in something means it sits inside it

blocks.note: an opus is a work, especially a musical one
a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: Coming up with the label for an intricate idea that appears in a piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like an adjective but is Freud's term for a pattern of repressed feelings.
explanation.definitionFit: Freud named the Oedipus complex after the Greek king who unknowingly killed his father and married his mother.

clue.text: Hint of raw power, passing leader, coming up in rowing event

indicators.note: a hint is only a trace, so just the first letter of the word is used
passing by the leader means going without it, so the first letter is dropped
coming up in a down clue means rising from bottom to top, read backwards

blocks.note: first letter of raw
wattage is power measured in watts

explanation.surface: A burst of raw strength, overtaking the front boat, rising at a rowing race.
explanation.definitionFit: A regatta is a series of boat races, especially rowing or sailing, held as a single event.

clue.text: Bustles around producing drink

indicators.note: turned around, the word is read from its last letter back to its first

blocks.note: ados are fusses or bustles of activity

explanation.surface: Busy flurries of activity at the bar result in a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink or soda water, a common mixer.

clue.text: Bridge player's stumble in form of poker?

definitions.note: strip names a form of poker only in strip poker, hence the question mark

blocks.note: S is South, one of the four bridge players
to trip is to stumble

explanation.surface: A card player slips up while playing a version of poker.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players are named by compass points: North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: In strip poker the losers of hands remove clothing, so strip is the word that names that variety.

clue.text: A hint about Tory's initial opinion – it's less than right

indicators.note: an initial is the first letter of a name or word, so only that letter is taken
one piece goes about, or around, another, enclosing it

blocks.note: a cue is a hint or prompt
first letter of Tory
an angle is a point of view on something

explanation.surface: A hint about a Conservative's view – which is a little short of correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like 'correct' but is a right angle of 90 degrees; the dash before it splits wordplay from definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An acute angle measures under 90 degrees, so it is smaller than a right angle.

clue.text: Bargain flags hoisted

indicators.note: hoisted in a down clue means lifted upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: on a golf course the flags on the greens are the pins

explanation.surface: A cheap deal on flags that have been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: A snip is British slang for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal usage a snip is something sold cheaply, a bargain.

clue.text: A lot of damage around a depression in Pacific island

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the last letter is dropped
what goes around another piece encloses it

blocks.note: to ruin is to damage
taken as written
a pan is a hollow or depression in the ground, as in a salt pan

explanation.surface: Widespread destruction surrounds a low-pressure system over an ocean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapa Nui is the Polynesian name for Easter Island, in the south-eastern Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Company taken aback about moist flowing in regard to liquid transfusion

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the letters run in reverse
flowing letters are fluid and move about into a new order
one piece placed about another wraps around it

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A firm is startled by damp seeping through during a fluid transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmotic relates to osmosis, the passage of a liquid solvent through a membrane, a kind of transfusion of fluid.

clue.text: Put off following American writer after inclusion of name

indicators.note: once something is included it sits inside, so the single letter goes into the writer

blocks.note: post is Latin for after, used as a prefix meaning following
Edgar Allan Poe, the American author
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A US author is deferred once a name has been added in.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to put off an event until later, a straight synonym for delay.

clue.text: Quantities of paper associated with a submission to publisher?

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
taken as written
MS is a manuscript, which an author submits to a publisher

explanation.surface: Masses of sheets go with a manuscript sent off to be published.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a standard quantity of paper, 500 sheets, and reams means large amounts of writing.
